subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Mince Words

options.text: To find a way to deal with something.

solution: The correct answer is **Option 3)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Mince Words"** means to speak vaguely or indirectly, often to avoid offending someone or to be polite. (घुमा फिरा कर बोलना) • **Example: **The manager didn't** mince words** when he gave feedback; he was straightforward and clear about the issues. • **"To speak vaguely or indirectly"** refers to not being direct or clear in communication, often to soften the impact of what is being said. (घुमा फिरा कर बोलना) • **Example: **Instead of telling her directly that she was late, he** minced words **and mentioned the importance of punctuality. Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is **'To speak vaguely or indirectly.**' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Almost failing **(लगभग असफल होना): To come very close to failing but not completely. • **Example:** He was **almost failing** his exams, but he managed to pass with some last-minute studying. • **To find a way to deal with something **(किसी चीज़ से निपटने का तरीका खोजना): To discover or create a method to handle a situation. • **Example: **She** found a way to deal with** her workload by prioritizing her tasks. • **Work not done for money** (पैसे के लिए नहीं किया गया काम): Labor or tasks performed without monetary compensation, often voluntarily. • **Example:** He spent his weekends doing community service**, work not done for money.** 32:Tb95, The correct answer is **Option 4)**
